query: Current NWS forecast for Death Valley Furnace Creek daily high temperatures July 11-23 2026, and any heat ridge/heat dome building in second half of July 2026 for Death Valley California
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Death Valley (Furnace Creek) — July 11–23, 2026 Forecast & Heat Ridge

**NWS Official Forecast (Furnace Creek, issued ~Jul 18):**
- Jul 18: ~116°F | Jul 19: ~117°F | Jul 20: ~115°F | Jul 21: ~117°F | Jul 22: ~118°F | Jul 23–24: 116–119°F
- Overnight lows stay dangerously warm at 98–100°F
- Note: July 11–17 are already in the past relative to the July 18 issuance; the current NWS product covers July 18 onward only

**Model guidance** shows heat intensifying beyond the window — climbing to ~119–120°F by Jul 24–27 and toward 124–126°F by Jul 28–29.

**Heat ridge / heat dome (CONFIRMED building in second half of July):**
- **Weather West** described "exceptionally broad and persistent west-central U.S. ridging" with "record-breaking" ridge intensity over parts of the West
- **CPC 6–10 & 8–14 day outlooks** favor above-normal temps at >60% probability across the Southwest/southern California due to "continuation of anomalous ridging"
- **CPC Probabilistic Hazards Outlook** (valid Jul 25–31) calls for a "westward shifting and strengthening area of mid-level high pressure," with a **moderate extreme-heat risk for the Desert Southwest July 25–28** (desert lows-elevation highs above 110°F)

**Bottom line:** The ridge is strengthening, not easing, into late July — favoring intensifying heat in the Death Valley region. The July 18–24 forecast (115–119°F) sits at-to-slightly-above the July climatological average (~116–117°F), with model projections pushing well above normal (120–126°F) in the final week of July.
